study_identification_part.si4_title: Dynamic gray matter volume changes in pediatric multiple sclerosis: A 3.5 year MRI study

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Assess spatial patterns of gray matter (GM) atrophy in pediatric multiple sclerosis (MS), characterize their longitudinal change (~3.5 years), and evaluate clinical relevance (disability, IQ) using deviations from age- and sex-expected GM trajectories.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Baseline: voxel-wise linear models (SPM12) related z-scores to EDSS, disease duration, IQ (full and subscales), and T1/T2 lesion volumes; longitudinal: linear models adjusted for follow-up duration, baseline EDSS, disease duration related z-score changes to baseline IQ and lesion volume changes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Pediatric MS shows widespread GM deviations from normative trajectories with progression notably in deep GM; deviations associate with greater disability and lesion burden, while higher IQ relates to reduced deviations.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: At baseline, patients showed significant negative deviations (z < 0) in multiple cortical and subcortical regions (e.g., thalamus L mean z −1.33, R −1.01; hippocampus L −1.41) with FWE correction. Over ~3.5 years, deviations progressed in bilateral thalamus (Δz ≈ −0.34 L; −0.35 R), hippocampus (L Δz −0.31; R −0.24), sensorimotor cortices, cingulate, precuneus, insula, and others (p < 0.001 uncorrected, cluster ≥50). Higher EDSS correlated with more negative z in thalamus/caudate/frontal and precuneus; longer disease duration correlated with more negative z in cingulate, frontal, temporal; higher IQ correlated with less negative z in cingulate, thalamus, and distributed cortical/cerebellar regions; greater T1/T2 lesion volumes correlated with more negative z in thalamus/caudate and frontal/temporal regions.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Lesion refilling performed prior to GM analysis; longitudinal SPM12+DARTEL pipeline; MFS covariate included in voxel-wise LME; IQ considered as cognitive reserve marker in association analyses.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: No explicit external or held-out validation of normative model; potential residual site/scanner effects not fully modeled beyond MFS covariate; relatively small longitudinal patient sample (n=30); ICV excluded (pediatric MS skull-brain dissociation) may impact comparability; NIH HC at 1.5T across centers whereas patient/HSR HC at 3T.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: All participants reported as Caucasian; scans for NIH HC acquired at six centers on GE/Siemens 1.5T; HSR scans at 3T Philips. Intracranial volume not included because skull/brain growth dissociation in pediatric MS. Data available on reasonable request.
